title: [decision] overlay `navigation.mode`: three renderers collapse four declared values into the drawer — and the measurement says portability is NOT the blocker, so this is a product question
body:
**Decision needed.** Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) at R31, as objectui#9113's triage comment requires: *"If the answer requires changing what the spec's enum means for these view types, that is a contract change and it goes to the decision box — a `needs-user-decision` card with the measurement attached. ⛔ A seat may not take it."*

The measurement round is **complete** (PR objectui#9296, report on objectui#9113). The delivering seat **declined to recommend**, correctly — the fence forbade a seat from choosing. This card carries the measurement, prices the routes, and adds a PM recommendation the maintainer can accept or discard.

## The question in one line

The spec publishes four overlay `navigation.mode` values. **`ObjectGantt`, `ObjectKanban` and `ObjectCalendar` collapse all four into the drawer**; `ObjectGrid` and `ObjectTree` honour them through `NavigationOverlay`. So the same authored metadata means different things depending on which view type reads it, with no diagnostic. **What should the four values mean on these surfaces?**

## ⭐ The measurement changes the shape of the question

**Question 1 — is the `Sheet` the container or the component? — is answered by execution: it is the CONTAINER.**

`RecordDetailDrawer`'s payload (`InlineEditProvider` → `DetailView`, plus `InlineEditSaveBar`) **renders in the modal, split and popover shells**, behind a lit drawer control. ⇒ **portability is not the constraint.** The question is a **product** one — what `split` and `popover` should *mean* on a gantt or a kanban — not a technical-feasibility one.

⚠️ **And one sub-premise of the original fence is corrected by measurement.** The fence listed four capabilities as blockers: record fetching, inline field save, lock handling, and a full-page href. **`RecordDetailDrawer` does not fetch the record.** I verified this myself rather than relaying it — `RecordDetailDrawerProps` declares `record: Record<string, any>` as a **required prop** and `objectSchema?` as an optional one (`packages/plugin-detail/src/RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:54-74`), with no fetch in the component. ⇒ of the four named blockers, **three travel inside the payload and the fourth is the caller's**. The "straight swap is not obviously available" premise is weaker than it looked.

## ⭐⭐ Two further narrowings, both verified independently at this seat

**1. `popover` is honoured NOWHERE — including on the two renderers this card calls correct.**

```
packages/components/src/custom/navigation-overlay.tsx   popoverTrigger declared, destructured, guarded, rendered  (5 hits)
packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:2228            a COMMENT: "Popover mode — uses NavigationOverlay Dialog fallback (no popoverTrigger)"
                                                        ⇒ ZERO renderers pass it
```

`NavigationOverlay` falls back to a compact `Dialog` when `popoverTrigger` is absent, and no renderer ever supplies one. ⇒ `popover` degrades to a Dialog on **five** surfaces, not three.

**2. On `ObjectTree`, an authored `split` renders NOTHING.** The split branch is `if (!isOpen || !mainContent) return null`, and `ObjectTree` never passes `mainContent` (`ObjectGrid` does, via a dedicated early return).

⇒ **the honest net picture: no renderer honours all four modes, and the two axes are anti-correlated.** The pair that honours `mode` renders the *poorer* payload; the three that collapse `mode` render the *rich* one. **Nobody gets both today.**

## The three routes, priced

| | route | what it costs |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **(a)** | **Honour the modes in all five renderers** | A payload/shell split at three call sites **plus an edit to `plugin-detail`** (`RecordDetailDrawer` brings its own `Sheet`). Chrome de-duplication that **moves the default drawer presentation on three published surfaces**. Reconciling two independent drag-resize implementations with different storage keys (`ov:KEY` vs `objectui.drawerWidth.OBJECT`) and different floors (**360 px vs 480 px**), so **existing users' persisted widths shift**. A structural change per renderer for `split`, which needs `mainContent`. A `popoverTrigger` that must be the clicked bar / card / event. And it must repair both narrowings above. ⚠️ **Blocked on the very product question this card asks.** |
| **(b)** | **Narrow the declared enum for these view types** (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove) | An `@objectstack/spec` change ⇒ a contract change by definition. Authoring-time rejection, migration for metadata already carrying these values, docs. Needs a shape that **does not exist yet** — a per-view-type mode vocabulary is a new kind of thing for this enum. ⚠️ **The measurement argues against it**: the payload is portable, so this narrows the contract to fit an implementation that **could** have met it. |
| **(c)** | **Keep the drawer, make the narrowing loud** | Much the cheapest — one shared helper, one call in each of three renderers, no spec change, no payload extraction, no chrome or resize reconciliation, no change to the default path. ⚠️ **But what it costs is a RULING, not work**: *refuse or warn?* A dev-only console warning changes nothing for a production author; a visible refusal is a **user-visible behaviour change on a published surface**, because today's drawer would stop appearing for anyone who authored `modal`. "Fall back to drawer but warn" is exactly today's code plus a log line. ⛔ And it leaves both narrowings unfixed — they are (a)-shaped. |

## ⭐ PM recommendation — **split the answer by mode**, because the modes are not alike

⚠️ Offered as a recommendation only; the decision is the maintainer's, and the three routes above stand unaltered if this is discarded.

The three values are lumped together by the card, but the measurement separates them:

- **`modal` has no product question at all.** It means "the same payload, centred, modal" — there is nothing to decide, and the measurement shows the payload already renders there. ⇒ **honour it** (route (a), restricted to one mode). Still not free: it needs the payload/shell split and touches `plugin-detail`. But it avoids **every** cost that is `split`- or `popover`- or resize-specific.
- **`split` and `popover` have no agreed meaning on a gantt, a kanban or a calendar** — what is the "main content" beside a split record panel on a kanban board? what element is the popover anchored to? ⇒ **route (c) for these two**, loud, until someone decides what they mean.
- ⭐ And **(c) applied to `popover` is close to free-standing value on its own**, because popover is honoured on **no** surface — so making it loud is honest everywhere rather than a special case for three renderers.

⇒ this gets the unambiguous mode working, stops the silent lie on the two ambiguous ones, and ⛔ does not spend a spec change on a limitation the implementation could have met.

**On refuse-vs-warn, if (c) is taken:** recommend **warn in development, fall back in production** — a visible refusal removes a working drawer from authors who did nothing wrong, and the drawer is a *reasonable* answer to `modal`, just not the declared one.

## Where the evidence is

- **PR objectui#9296** — the measurement, 5 test files, +992/−0, **no product source touched**. `Test Files 4 passed / Tests 30 passed`.
- **objectui#9113** — the card, its binding triage comment, and the seat's full report.
- ⭐ The instrument caught itself once and it is worth noting: the question-1 probe's **lit control failed on the first run** (a network escape to `localhost:3000`, plus an over-loose assertion), which was read as **NOT MEASURED** rather than as a negative answer, repaired, and re-run green.

## Blocked

objectui#9113 cannot be retired without this ruling. Both narrowings above are inputs to it rather than separable repairs, so ⛔ neither was filed as its own card.

⚠️ **Dedup gap, named:** REST `/search/issues` is proxy-refused in this session, so dedup ran over **open** issues only (450 read, objectui#9113 itself as the lit control). A closed duplicate would not have been seen.

Refs: objectui#9113 · PR objectui#9296 · objectui#7334 · objectui#7210 (route B, unruled, ⛔ out of scope) · objectui#7742 · ADR-0049
